evals.prompt: Set up a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline for our TypeScript Express API. We use PostgreSQL, run tests with Jest, build a Docker image, and deploy to AWS ECS. We want PR checks and auto-deploy to staging on merge to main, with manual approval for production.
evals.expected_output: Should produce a complete GitHub Actions workflow with lint, test (with Postgres service), build Docker image, deploy to staging, and gated production deploy. Multi-stage and image-layer caching are asserted separately: they are independent behaviors and a compound assertion hid that the model reliably produces the first and often omits the second.
assertions: Lint and test run in parallel
PostgreSQL service container configured with health check
Dependencies are cached
Docker build uses a multi-stage Dockerfile (a build stage that compiles, a slim runtime stage carrying only the artifact)
Docker image layers are cached across runs (buildx cache-from/cache-to, or an equivalent registry/gha layer cache)
Staging deploys automatically on main push
Production deploy requires manual approval (environment protection)
Smoke test after each deployment
All jobs have timeouts
Action versions are pinned

evals.prompt: Our CI pipeline takes 35 minutes. It runs lint, unit tests, integration tests, e2e tests, security scan, build, and deploy all sequentially. How can we speed it up?
evals.expected_output: Should identify parallelization opportunities, caching improvements, and suggest restructuring. Should not suggest skipping tests.
assertions: Identifies that lint, unit tests, and security scan can run in parallel
Recommends dependency caching
Suggests splitting integration and e2e tests from unit tests
Does NOT suggest removing or skipping tests
Recommends concurrency control to cancel outdated runs
Provides a restructured pipeline diagram

evals.prompt: We publish our SDK to npm from GitHub Actions. Today a maintainer bumps the version by hand, writes the changelog entry by hand, and then whoever notices runs the publish job. We've shipped a wrong version twice. I want one reliable process — sort it out.
evals.expected_output: Two different kinds of decision are tangled in one request and the roster does not separate them. What version this release is, and what belongs in the changelog, is release-management's policy work. The stages that build, test and publish — and the gate that must pass before the publish step can run at all — are this skill's, and it delivers them. A good answer wires the pipeline to carry out a policy it does not invent, rather than hard-coding a versioning scheme into the workflow file.
assertions: Separates the two halves: deciding what version a release gets and what goes in the changelog, versus wiring the steps that build and publish it
Refers to release-management for the versioning scheme and changelog generation
Delivers the pipeline half itself — the stages and the gate that must pass before publish can run — rather than deferring the whole request
Does not invent a versioning scheme or a changelog format inside the workflow file
States the boundary: release management decides what a release is, while the pipeline is what carries it out
